framing_issues.text: Counting more of the money toward fuel would raise their fuel charge
framing_issues.issue: In the 30-second version, which most readers see, the effect is reversed. The record (P-066, P-105) says a bigger fuel credit lowers the fuel charge, so this makes the change look harmful to the readers it would help.

framing_issues.text: Georgia Power tried to silence parts of GIPL's testimony
framing_issues.issue: Loaded, unequal verb. 'Silence' casts a routine motion to strike (P-134) as suppression, while GIPL's reply on line 31 gets the neutral 'asked'. Use 'asked the PSC to strike'.

framing_issues.text: a typical home's bill would drop by about $1.84 a month
framing_issues.issue: Beyond being wrong, $1.84 flips the comparison. Next to $1.65 on the base side it suggests a fuel-side shift helps homes on net. Georgia Power's figures ($1.48 vs $1.65, P-142/P-143; line 208) imply the opposite.

framing_issues.text: GAM said:
framing_issues.issue: Misattributing PIA Staff's words to GAM makes GAM look like an opponent of Georgia Power's pipeline plan. It also contradicts line 182, which gives the same quote to PIA Staff.

framing_issues.text: GAM witness Jonathan Ly said no part of real-time revenue should be credited against these fees
framing_issues.issue: Placed under 'Who says it' on the card for Georgia Power's pipeline plan. GAM's point (no real-time revenue credited against FT) conflicts with that plan, which books real-time revenue to fuel to cover new FT (P-127). This overstates GAM's alignment with Georgia Power.

framing_issues.text: PIA Staff found Georgia Power could have absorbed the larger fuel credit
framing_issues.issue: Unequal verbs: Staff 'found' (a finding), while other parties 'say' or 'said'. The next sentence, 'So base rates would not necessarily rise', then adopts Staff's conclusion in the page's own voice.

framing_issues.text: None of the four parties whose testimony we archived asks to keep it unchanged
framing_issues.issue: Missing context. Georgia Power 'argues that the current method is fair' (P-099, per GIPL). GAM accepts change only conditionally and opposes crediting real-time revenue to FT (P-110, P-111). 'Who supports it: None' understates support for parts of today's method.

framing_issues.text: Georgia Power and GIPL say real-time customers should carry only costs they can change
framing_issues.issue: Puts a general principle in GIPL's mouth that GIPL rejects for pipeline, coal-related and overhead costs (P-096, P-101, P-156). This misrepresents GIPL's overall position.

framing_issues.text: PIA Staff estimates Option 2 alone would add about $126 million to the credit in 2026
framing_issues.issue: Uneven caveats. Option C's benefits carry Staff's dollar figures, with no note here that Staff calls its data incomplete (P-078) or that the page-7 figures ($329M, $322M, $1.35; P-066) were open to the Oct 7 errata ('page 7, line 9', P-039). Options B and D show no numbers because Georgia Power's are blacked out, so Option C can look bigger by comparison.

framing_issues.text: "Supported" means the case record or a party's own figures back the claim
framing_issues.issue: Labeling a claim 'Supported' when only the proponent's own figures back it can read as independent confirmation (cards 1, 2 and 6).

framing_issues.text: Customers on standard rates keep paying the fixed fuel costs left out of the credit
framing_issues.issue: The page's own voice adopts PIA Staff's framing (P-063, 'absorbing all these costs'). Georgia Power's counterpoint that base-side revenue offsets these costs (P-124) appears only under 'What's uncertain'.

framing_issues.text: "Mixed" means parties give credible but conflicting accounts
framing_issues.issue: 'Credible' is an unexamined judgment applied to every party.

framing_issues.text: PIA Staff said its approach is
framing_issues.issue: Uneven naming. Card 2 names all three Staff witnesses and a date. Cards 3 to 5 often say only 'Georgia Power's witnesses' (line 171), 'PIA Staff said' (lines 183-186) or 'GIPL's witness' (line 195), with no date, though all are labeled 'Documented' (named-witness rule, line 138).

framing_issues.text: Big businesses on real-time pricing pay one hourly price for their extra power
framing_issues.issue: 'Big' overstates. RTP-DA is open to commercial and industrial customers from 250 kW of demand, about 2,300 customers (P-044). It also clashes with line 59's 'Any business customer can choose it'.

framing_issues.text: Stan Wise joined the PSC on Sep 5, 2026
framing_issues.issue: Missing context: Wise was first elected to the PSC in 1994 and stepped down in 2018 (P-033, P-034). 'Joined' suggests he is new.

framing_issues.text: Homes pay 58.07% of base revenues but 55.36% of fuel revenues, by a cost study GAM cited
framing_issues.issue: Missing context: the shares come from a cost study for a test year ending July 31, 2023 (P-116), cited by GAM, an interested party.

framing_issues.text: it should have used the "associated interchange energy rate" instead
framing_issues.issue: Technical term left unexplained.

framing_issues.text: Georgia Power asked the PSC to strike that part of GIPL's testimony
framing_issues.issue: 'Strike' (remove from the record) is not explained.

framing_issues.text: using each group's share of winter peak growth to split the fees
framing_issues.issue: Allocation terms are unexplained: 'winter peak growth' and 'peak-based split' (lines 108, 116, 170), and 'split the way transmission costs are split' (line 124).

framing_issues.text: such as gas hedging gains and losses
framing_issues.issue: Unexplained jargon. Similar terms: 'monthly access charge' (line 62), 'Administrative Session' (line 40) and 'proposed orders' (line 38).
